conclusion: Organic branch topology and independent output layers use different Z grids: clip output slices and propagated roots using belt-floor polygons evaluated at each output layer's physical print_z, not the topology cache index, and keep a positive regular height for negative-Z layer zero. Parallel overhang sampling can emit tips and roofs onto shared lower layers; quantized tip deduplication must publish layer-local candidates in stable source-layer order rather than mutex acquisition order. Otherwise even fresh slices with identical settings can generate different support geometry, and support-only re-slices differ from a fresh slice. Lower continuous roof footprints must retain their parent contact and depth until the output grid is known, then map to contact output index minus depth. Flooring aggregated topology-Z interface layers can omit a complete interface immediately below an exact contact. Preserve source-index placement on synchronized fallback. Current endpoint fixes additionally lower the independent bed-support layer only when necessary to preserve a nearby exact contact within minimum thickness constraints. Historical Benchy timing and path-comparison observations are not current-build guarantees. The generic G-code layer-count fix filters empty export records and shares one plan for counting and generation. Support geometry and contact-height algorithms are unchanged, and current support and belt regressions pass.
